entities.summary: Lajos Thallóczy was a Hungarian historian, a politician and diplomat, the head of the joint finance department of the Dual Monarchy, a member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, the president of the Hungarian Historical Society from 1913 to 1916 and a renowned albanologist. As a diplomat in Austria-Hungary he played a very significant role in the Balkans as he was considered an expert on the history of the region. He was one of the most important advisers to Gyula Andrássy and Béni Kállay in questions of Balkan policy and even to the emperor Franz Joseph and to the minister of the government.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a renowned albanologist and expert on Balkan history, Lajos Thallóczy played a significant role in shaping Austria-Hungary's policy towards the region, advising key figures such as Gyula Andrássy and Béni Kállay. His expertise had regional implications, contributing to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the Balkans during this period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a diplomat in Austria-Hungary, Lajos Thallóczy played a significant role in Balkan policy, advising key figures such as Gyula Andrássy and Béni Kállay. His expertise on the region's history influenced imperial decisions, contributing to the complex web of alliances that shaped the region during this period.
